We are starting the private deployment evaluation for Acme's tenant (prod-tn-17) and need a concise checklist for networking and architecture pre-reqs. Specifically:
- VPC peering or private interconnect options
- Required firewall/egress rules and CIDR ranges
- Service mesh / ingress recommendations for our multi-AZ setup
- Any HSM/KMS requirements for keys and certs

I attached our current network diagram (acme-network-diagram.vsdx) — it's still a draft. Can your onboarding team confirm what we should prepare before the infra kickoff next week? Also please include any timing estimates and who from Redwood we should expect on the call.

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the diagram — this is exactly the kind of context we need. We can run the infra kickoff on Feb 12; proposed attendees from Redwood: myself (solutions engineer), Marissa Cole (infra lead), and Kimberly Park (network intake).

Attached is a concise checklist we use for private deployments (redwood-private-onboard-checklist-v0.1.pdf). High-level items:
- VPC/subnet layout & routing intent (CIDRs, NAT, IGW/egress)
- VPN or Direct Connect / Cloud Interconnect details (peerings, ASN, BGP ranges)
- Firewall rules and required outbound CIDRs for model telemetry & control plane
- Service account and service principal creation + IAM roles
- KMS/HSM integration notes and cert delivery method
- Proxy/ingress (recommendations for Envoy or cloud-native ingress + TLS termination)

Two quick asks before kickoff:
1) Can you confirm the expected egress IPs for your tenant (if using NAT) or whether you'll use BGP announced ranges?
2) Do you require on-prem HSM connections for keys or will you use cloud KMS?

I'll follow up with a calendar invite for Feb 12 10:00 AM PT.

Best,

Alex / Sofia,

Quick notes from the infra side to add to the checklist before the kickoff:
- Service mesh: if Acme wants mTLS between host-level services and Redwood sidecars, we'll need cert distribution and rotation windows documented. For most customers we recommend Envoy + SDS; if using cloud-managed meshes we can adapt.
- KV cache and model shard placement: confirm egress latency SLA (we target <5ms intra-AZ for cache hits). This impacts AZ placement and peering topology.
- Ingress: prefer a dedicated ALB/NLB in front with path-based routing to keep control-plane and data-plane separated.
- Health checks: list of ports (see firewall-ports-reference.txt) — include TCP 1024-65535 ephemeral ranges if using certain container runtimes.

I'll bring the service-mesh runbook to the kickoff.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Infra Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Thanks Marissa — good context. To answer Alex's questions:
- Egress: we'll be using a NAT gateway per AZ, so Acme will provide an egress CIDR set ahead of time (we'll share during the kickoff).
- KMS/HSM: we plan to use our on-prem HSM for key custody for production; test/staging can use cloud KMS. We will need clear instructions for TLS cert import and rotation frequency.

I've uploaded an updated network drawing to the shared folder (see link) and attached a short firewall rules export for our edge routers. Can someone confirm whether Redwood needs inbound access from your control plane, or if all control plane communications are outbound from the tenant?

Looking forward to Feb 12.

Sofia

2) Kickoff agenda (Feb 12, 10:00 AM PT):
   - Introductions and success criteria (10 min)
   - Network topology and routing (15 min)
   - Firewall/NAT and egress rules (15 min)
   - KMS/HSM integration approach (20 min)
   - Service mesh/ingress options and HA considerations (20 min)

3) Security/control-plane note: Redwood's control plane initiates outbound connections for agent registration and metrics collection. We do not require inbound access to customer VPCs. If your policies require mutual TLS with a pinned certificate, we can support that; bring HSM details to the HSM subsection of the kickoff.

4) Attachments provided here for ease of reference: redwood-private-onboard-checklist-v0.1.pdf, firewall-ports-reference.txt.

If that looks good I'll send the calendar invite and a short Confluence notes page after the call.
